# ObjOrthoRender

> Render textured 3D OBJ meshes into georeferenced GeoTIFF orthophotos (DOM). Batch processing, multiprocessing, multi-level merging, and a headless Docker image that runs without a GPU.

ObjOrthoRender is a command-line tool and Tkinter GUI that turns a directory of
textured `.obj` meshes plus a `metadata.xml` (SRS + SRSOrigin) into georeferenced
GeoTIFF orthophotos. It is the "mesh to 2D map" step of a photogrammetry
pipeline, typically applied to the OBJ output of a 3D Tiles conversion.

Key capabilities: block-wise rendering to bypass GPU memory and texture size
limits; three merge strategies (`all`, `subfolder`, `none`); hole filling tuned
for water surfaces; multiprocessing across OBJ files; and a Docker image with
Xvfb + Mesa software OpenGL so it runs on servers with no discrete GPU.

## Entry points

- `render_orthophotos.py` - rendering core and CLI entry point. Flags: `--input`,
  `--output`, `--metadata`, `--gsd`, `--workers`, `--merge-mode`, `--fill-holes`,
  `--subdir`.
- `gui_app.py` - Tkinter desktop GUI.
- `Dockerfile` - headless image, defaults to `/data` as the input mount point.
- `build_exe.py` - PyInstaller packaging for Windows.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/UVE1048/ObjOrthoRender/blob/main/README.md): features, parameters, output layout, comparison with alternatives, FAQ.
- [Usage guide](https://github.com/UVE1048/ObjOrthoRender/blob/main/docs/usage.md): detailed Docker and GUI parameter reference.

## Input and output contract

Input: a directory tree containing `.obj` files (recursive), their `.mtl` and
textures, and a `metadata.xml` with `<SRS>` and `<SRSOrigin>`.
Output: RGB GeoTIFF (no alpha, black background) placed next to your chosen
output directory, optionally merged into `MergedDOM/merged_all.tif`.
